reported.title: Pump output chatters because there is no hysteresis or debounce
reported.description: The control logic at lines 71-78 uses a single threshold (START_CM = 45.0) with no stop threshold and no hysteresis band, so any reading below 45.0 immediately calls setPump(false) and any reading at or above it calls setPump(true). Because sampleLevelCm() (lines 22-24) is a raw single ADC read with no filtering or debounce, sensor noise near the threshold flips the output on every 40 ms poll. The measurements confirm this: 64 toggles in a 5000 ms window during threshold hover, 34 during rapid oscillation, and 8 during a brief glitch spike, all far above the limit of 2. D7 toggled 64 times in a 5000 ms window starting at 1.32 s (limit 2), and 84 times over the whole 8.00 s run.

judge_input.spec:
- Linear water-level sensor on A1 at 10 mV/cm; sump pump contactor on D7; silence pushbutton on D4 to ground with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- Start the pump when level reaches 45.0 cm or higher; stop the pump when level falls to 30.0 cm or lower.
- Holding D4 LOW latches silence mode and keeps the pump OFF until reset (power cycle).
- Pump output must not toggle more than 2 times in any 5000 ms window.
- Every 800 ms print `sump cm=<level> pump=<0|1> mute=<0|1>` with level to one decimal place.
- Apply pump start/stop within 500 ms of a sustained band crossing.
